Notification settings

Session only. Opening the app does not share AURA measurements. Audio plays on request using fixed narration scripts; no measurements are included in these voice requests. Internet required.

How these prototype rules work

Rest: eligible sleep below the entered target plus resting HR more than one robust baseline deviation above reference. Mindfulness: that HR change plus HRV more than one robust deviation below reference. These are AURA design thresholds, not NASA-validated or clinical cutoffs. Resting data must pass the existing five-minute quality gate, be under 24 hours old, and have a matching baseline of at least seven prior days. Activity: current recorded units below planned units, which may simply reflect an unfinished day. Bone: a reminder for any modeled mission day above zero; never a bone-density measurement. Dismissals last until reload, clear, or mode change. No alert does not establish safety.

          SIM-01 reports dizziness during a scheduled activity. Practice observation recording, communication status and handover. This script is an AURA-authored workflow demonstration, not a validated emergency procedure. No diagnosis or treatment is provided.

            How this interpretation works
            Descriptions use the existing readiness inputs. Review prompts use the prototype’s one-standardized-unit HR/HRV deviations or sleep below the entered target.             TRANSPARENT ASSUMPTIONS
            Mission scenario
            NASA RAD · January 2024
            Historical observations from Curiosity on Mars. Choose a UTC date range from the bundled seven-day excerpt.
            Dose is estimated only between adjacent accepted observations, up to 45 minutes apart. Rejected observations break the curve.
            Import a different radiation series
            Required columns: timestamp,dose_rate_uGy_per_day. Trapezoidal integration; gaps over 36 hours are excluded. Preserve the source’s detector/material and quality flags when preparing the CSV. This custom importer is separate from the NASA-specific quality pipeline.
            NASA bone-health reference
            Published rate reference: 1–2% per month
            Context: absence of effective countermeasures. This is not an estimate of your response to exercise.
            AURA assumes linear change: index = 100 − rate × days / 30. Baseline 100 is normalized, not a DXA measurement. The 180-day cap limits extrapolation; it is not a validated horizon.
            Wearable activity cannot establish bone density. Exercise adherence stays separate from this reference. Lunar/Mars gravity and postflight recovery are outside its scope.

            NASA DATA & RESOURCE PROVENANCE
            Where the evidence comes from
            RADIATION INTEGRATED
            

            OBSERVATIONS USED
            Curiosity / RAD radiation
            NASA SPDF/CDAWeb Level 2 files, version 04, 1–7 January 2024 UTC. Channel: Total Dose E in DOSIMETRY_TOTAL — tissue-equivalent plastic. 591 observations; 574 accepted and 17 rejected in the bundled excerpt.
            AURA removes quality-flagged or invalid measurements, then estimates cumulative absorbed dose using trapezoidal integration over accepted neighboring observations. No interpolation across rejected data or gaps over 45 minutes. µGy/day → accumulated mGy; no conversion to mSv.
            NASA dataset catalog ↗Original CDF archive ↗Download excerpt, metadata & source checksums ↓
            Credit: RAD PI Dr. Donald M. Hassler, Southwest Research Institute, Boulder; RAD team; NASA/JPL MSL; NASA SPDF/CDAWeb. Retrieved 14 November 2026.
            

            RESEARCH PARAMETERS USED
            Bone-health reference
            NASA Glenn reports 1–2% monthly bone-density loss without effective countermeasures. NASA’s Bone and Mineral Laboratory describes hip/spine loss and DXA monitoring. AURA uses these published rates, not individual astronaut records.
            The two curves apply constant rates linearly to an index of 100. The shaded span is a scenario range, not a confidence interval. Modern exercise countermeasures may change outcomes; this model does not quantify their benefit or predict personal fracture risk.
            NASA Musculoskeletal · rate source ↗NASA Bone and Mineral Laboratory · context ↗Download parameters, assumptions & sources ↓
            Sources accessed 14 November 2026. Bone reference is excluded from Daily Readiness and does not constitute a validated Mission Health Score.
            

            PIPELINE REPLAY · ECG EXCERPT
            Flight-crew physiology
            A real ECG excerpt from NASA’s pilot benchmark recordings is processed locally through an experimental beat detector and AURA’s existing SignalWindow filter and summary code.
            This ground-based recording is not astronaut spaceflight data. One excerpt tests execution and data handling; it does not validate readiness, attention classification, medical accuracy or Bluetooth hardware.

            EVIDENCE & TESTING
            What AURA has tested
            Engineering results are separate from your personal health record. NASA recordings exercise the processing code; they do not establish clinical accuracy.
            Open NASA ECG processing test
            NASA FLIGHT-CREW · ENGINEERING TEST
            Recorded ECG → AURA processing
            SEPARATE FROM PERSONAL DATA
            Replay one 310-second, 256 Hz ground-benchmark excerpt. AURA detects candidate beats, derives RR intervals and HR, then runs the same quality filters and five-minute summary used by the sensors. No personal baseline or readiness score is created.
            Not run in this session.
            HR and RMSSD below are experimental estimates from detected peaks, not annotated reference values. Insufficient-quality output remains unavailable. Rejections may include artifacts, real physiological changes or detector errors.
            What this test establishes
            Checks ECG ingestion, timing, derived interval handling, rejection rules, coverage and summary generation on real data. It does not test Bluetooth transport, validate wearable accuracy or establish clinical accuracy. The source has event labels, not annotated R peaks; no sensitivity or error claim is made. The fixed detector is a prototype heuristic, not a validated ECG algorithm.
            AURA Personal Health Model · Hackathon prototype v0.9 · Guidance, reassessment & evidence
            Cloud questions share selected health data with OpenAI. Radiation is historical; bone is modeled. Medical Assist is a fictional training simulation; clinical emergency assistance and automated medical alerts are not implemented.
            Readiness scoring methodology
            Daily readiness: 30% HR, 30% RMSSD, 25% sleep, 15% exercise adherence. Missing domains are excluded; a score requires resting HR, sleep and at least one other domain. Weights and display bands are unvalidated design choices. SpO₂, bone reference and NASA radiation are not averaged into this score. Coverage is not statistical confidence.
